statement: Bake geometry into the Rhino model with layer, name, colour and user-text key-value attributes in one step.
superiority: Dino 8 bakes with undo as a single step and reports attributes that could not be applied.

acceptance.corpus: 1000 curves baked with layer, name and 5 user-text keys
acceptance.tolerance: All 1000 objects carry the correct attributes; one undo removes all

statement: Define a reusable attribute set holding layer, colour, name and any number of user-text pairs that can be attached to geometry.
superiority: Dino 8 offers a visible attribute schema with types and defaults.

acceptance.corpus: Attribute set with 20 keys applied to 100 objects
acceptance.tolerance: Every object reads back all 20 keys with identical values

statement: Reference model objects into the definition by matching user-text keys and values.
superiority: Dino 8 indexes user text so lookups are instant on large models.

acceptance.tolerance: Query returns exactly matching objects; time under 200 ms

statement: Reference model objects by layer, name, object type, colour and other Rhino attributes with wildcards.
superiority: Dino 8 supports combined logical queries and live updates on model edits.

acceptance.corpus: Model with nested layers and 50k objects
acceptance.tolerance: Result set equals reference filter; wildcard patterns case behaviour documented and tested

statement: Read all user-text keys and values from referenced objects as ordered lists.
superiority: Dino 8 preserves insertion order and value types.

acceptance.corpus: Objects with 30 keys in a set order
acceptance.tolerance: Key order and values identical to authored

statement: Read Rhino object attributes such as layer, colour, material and visibility for referenced objects.
superiority: Dino 8 returns typed fields directly with no parsing.

acceptance.tolerance: All attribute fields equal the document values

statement: Change attributes and user text on existing model objects, including blocks, without re-baking geometry.
superiority: Dino 8 edits in place with full undo and no geometry rewrite.

acceptance.corpus: 1000 existing objects with changed layer and a user-text key
acceptance.tolerance: Geometry GUIDs unchanged; attributes updated; single undo restores

statement: Create and update block definitions and instances from Grasshopper geometry with user text on both definition and instance.
superiority: Dino 8 updates definitions in place and preserves instance attributes.

acceptance.corpus: Update a block definition used by 500 instances
acceptance.tolerance: All instances reflect the change; instance user text preserved

statement: Reference block instances and their nested geometry with transforms resolved.
superiority: Dino 8 explodes nested blocks lazily and preserves hierarchy paths.

acceptance.tolerance: Geometry placed at the correct world transform within 1e-9

statement: Attach attributes to geometry that is not yet baked so data travels with it through the definition.
superiority: Dino 8 carries data natively on geometry with no wrapper type.

acceptance.corpus: Branch of 100 curves with attached keys passed through transforms
acceptance.tolerance: Keys remain on each output; baked results read back equal

statement: Treat the model as a queryable database where each object has an identity and relationships usable for analysis.
superiority: Dino 8 offers a native object table with indexed fields.

acceptance.tolerance: Join/filter query results equal an independent script; under 500 ms

statement: Bake geometry into a controlled layer hierarchy with automatic creation and clean-up.
superiority: Dino 8 creates and recolours layers atomically with undo.

acceptance.corpus: Bake to 40 nested layers named by a data tree
acceptance.tolerance: Layer tree equals the authored paths; duplicates absent
